page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs using the x86_64 architecture, specifically utilizing the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.hfc6.16xlarge demonstrates strong capabilities in specific memory and instruction-set tasks. It achieves a strong rating in memory bandwidth for read-only large blocks at 209.21 GB/sec and in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 269.5 GB/sec. Passmark CPU extended instructions and database operations also score in the top 25% tier. However, the instance exhibits weak performance in large language model text generation, scoring in the bottom 25% for both 135M and 7B models. Most other general compute, single-core, and multi-core benchmarks fall within the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high clock speed make this instance suitable for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring external block storage attachments, and the low memory-to-vCPU ratio. This configuration is well-suited for high-throughput database operations, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and compute-intensive applications such as software compilation and physics simulations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY vCPUs operating at 3.1 GHz and 128.0 GB of RAM. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 20 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark data highlights strong performance in large-block read-only memory bandwidth, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Passmark database operations. Conversely, it shows weak performance in LLM text generation. With a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core, the instance represents a specialized compute-heavy profile. It is best suited for multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and CPU-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage.
